verdict.rationale: Aider is itself an AI coding assistant. Users delegate natural-language tasks to it inside the chat. It can figure out which files to edit, apply the edits, auto-commit them, and run lint and tests. Delegation also works through /ask, /architect, voice, watch-mode AI! comments and one-shot --message scripting. Community users confirm it delivers on real codebases. Missing for 10: first-party documented autonomous multi-step agent mode (the 'navigator-mode' autonomy is a community add-on, not core Aider).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: You can use aider without adding any files, and it will try to figure out which files need to be edited based on your requests.
Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
AI! triggers aider to make changes to your code.
Request new features, test cases or bug fixes using your voice and let aider do the work of editing the files in your local git repo.
Then Aider delivered from the first prompt.
